name: balance_white's Protect/Unprotect guard stays correctly counted across sequential measurements
contract: BalanceWhiteGuard used to hold one process-wide protected set replaced wholesale by Protect()/Clear(); when two actors ran balance_white at the same time (as the balance suite does across lanes on one worldserver), one actor's Protect/Clear call could unprotect the other actor's victim mid-measurement, letting an unclamped swing kill it and hang the case until the scenario timeout (observed in the balance-35-20/40 exploratory smoke runs, failure_actors showing the fighter at health 0, out of combat). The guard now reference-counts guarded guids per call instead of replacing the whole set. CoAGameplayTest advances one step at a time per case (a single `_nextStep` cursor), so necro1's and necro2's balance_white steps below run strictly sequentially within this one case, never concurrently: this file alone does not reproduce the cross-case race the fix addresses, and would pass on both the pre-fix and post-fix guard if run in isolation. What it does prove: Protect()/Unprotect() stays correctly reference-counted across two consecutive, non-overlapping balance_white measurements against different victims in the same case (a reentrancy check on the same guard, distinct from the cross-case race). The cross-case race itself is exercised whenever this scenario and other balance_white scenarios (the per-spec dungeon cases) run concurrently across lanes during a full `tools/balance_suite.py run` or a multi-scenario `--stages gameplay` batch — that is how the implementer actually reproduced and verified the fix, by running this file alongside balance-35-20/40/60 together, not by running it alone.
